subject: Geography
topic: Rivers of India — Origin, Course and Tributaries

questions.text: The Ganga river originates from which glacial source in Uttarakhand?

options.text: Yamunotri glacier — source of the Yamuna River
Gangotri glacier (Gomukh) — source of the Bhagirathi
Chorabari glacier — source of the Mandakini River
Milam glacier — source of the Goriganga tributary

questions.explanation: The Ganga originates at Gomukh ('cow's mouth'), the snout of the Gangotri glacier at ~3,900 m in Uttarakhand. The Bhagirathi River flows from Gangotri and is considered the principal headstream; it joins the Alaknanda at Devprayag to form the Ganga proper. The Yamunotri glacier is the source of the Yamuna, not the Ganga.

questions.text: The Brahmaputra River is known by which name as it flows through Tibet (China)?

options.text: Yarlung Tsangpo — its Tibetan name before the great bend
Jamuna — the name used for the river in Bangladesh downstream
Lohit — one of the Brahmaputra's Arunachal tributaries
Dibang — a major tributary that joins the Brahmaputra in Assam

questions.explanation: The Brahmaputra originates in Tibet as the Yarlung Tsangpo (also written Tsang Po). After making a dramatic hairpin turn (great bend) around Namcha Barwa peak, it enters Arunachal Pradesh as the Dihang, then becomes the Brahmaputra in Assam. In Bangladesh, it merges with the Ganga and is called the Jamuna.

questions.text: Most peninsular rivers flow eastward, but the Narmada flows westward into the Arabian Sea. What is the geological reason?

options.text: It originates in the Aravalli Range, which naturally slopes westward
It flows through a rift valley (graben) between the Vindhya and Satpura ranges
It was captured by the Indus drainage system during the Pleistocene
It follows the original westward drainage of Gondwana supercontinent

questions.explanation: The Narmada flows through a rift valley — an elongated depression formed by parallel faults — between the Vindhya Range (north) and Satpura Range (south). This structural graben channels it westward into the Gulf of Khambhat. The Tapi (Tapti) similarly flows west through its own rift valley. Other peninsular rivers draining east follow the tilt of the Deccan plateau.

questions.text: The Kaveri water dispute between Karnataka and Tamil Nadu exists primarily because ____.

options.text: Kaveri originates in Karnataka but its lower basin agriculture depends heavily on Tamil Nadu
Tamil Nadu built illegal upstream dams on the Kaveri without Karnataka's knowledge
The 1892 Cauvery Waters Agreement was declared void by the Supreme Court
Karnataka illegally diverts Kaveri water into the Krishna basin through canals

questions.explanation: The Kaveri originates in Karnataka (Coorg/Kodagu) but Tamil Nadu's delta agriculture — particularly the Thanjavur delta — has historically depended on its waters. Karnataka's development needs conflict with Tamil Nadu's historic water-use rights. The Cauvery Water Disputes Tribunal (1990) and a Supreme Court ruling (2018) attempted to apportion flows but disputes continue, especially during drought years.

questions.text: Which of the following rivers does NOT drain into the Bay of Bengal?

options.text: Mahanadi — flows through Odisha into the Bay of Bengal
Godavari — flows through Andhra Pradesh to the Bay of Bengal
Tapti (Tapi) — flows westward into the Gulf of Khambhat
Krishna — flows through Andhra Pradesh to the Bay of Bengal

questions.explanation: The Tapti (Tapi) flows westward through its rift valley and drains into the Gulf of Khambhat (Arabian Sea) near Surat, Gujarat. Mahanadi (Odisha), Godavari (AP/Telangana), and Krishna (AP) are all east-flowing peninsular rivers draining into the Bay of Bengal. West-flowing peninsular rivers are rarer: Narmada, Tapti, Periyar, Sharavati.

questions.text: The Indus river originates in Tibet and enters India through Ladakh. Near Mithankot in Pakistan, it receives ____.

options.text: Only the Chenab alone, which is the single largest tributary meeting there
The combined Panjnad — waters of all five Punjab rivers (Jhelum, Chenab, Ravi, Beas, Sutlej)
The Yamuna River, which was redirected westward following Siwalik Range tectonic uplift
The Beas alone, after the other four rivers join the Arabian Sea directly

questions.explanation: Near Mithankot (Pakistan), the Indus receives the Panjnad — the combined channel of the five Punjab rivers: Jhelum + Chenab (= Chenab), then Ravi, then Beas + Sutlej (= Sutlej), which all merge successively to form the Panjnad before joining the Indus. The Indus itself originates near Singi Khamban (Sengge Zangbo) in Tibet and enters India through Ladakh at Demchok.

questions.text: Which pairing of characteristics is CORRECTLY matched to the right river category?

options.text: Himalayan rivers: rain-fed only, non-perennial; Peninsular rivers: glacier-fed, perennial
Himalayan rivers: young, V-shaped gorges, high erosion; Peninsular rivers: old, graded, gentler gradient
Himalayan rivers: all flow west to the Arabian Sea; Peninsular rivers: all flow east to Bay of Bengal
Himalayan rivers: originate in Aravalli and Satpura; Peninsular rivers: originate in Himalayan glaciers

questions.explanation: Himalayan rivers are geologically young (post-Himalayan uplift, ~50 Ma), actively eroding, V-shaped valleys, and perennial (glacier + monsoon-fed). Peninsular rivers flow over ancient Gondwana rock, have graded profiles, wide flood plains, and are mostly rain-fed (seasonal). Option A reverses perenniality; Option C is wrong (Narmada, Tapti are westward peninsular rivers); Option D reverses the origins entirely.
